duzeltme.govde: A $1.00\text{ mol}$ sample of $\mathrm{CO_2}(g)$ is placed in a rigid $0.500\text{ L}$ container at $27\text{ °C}$. The measured pressure of the gas is significantly lower than the pressure predicted by the ideal gas law. Which of the following gives the pressure predicted by the ideal gas law and the best explanation for the difference? ($R=0.08206\text{ L·atm/(mol·K)}$)
duzeltme.secenekler[0].text: $4.43\text{ atm}$; attractions between $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecules reduce the force of their collisions with the walls.
duzeltme.secenekler[1].text: $12.3\text{ atm}$; attractions between $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecules reduce the force of their collisions with the walls.
duzeltme.secenekler[2].text: $49.2\text{ atm}$; the volume of the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecules reduces the free space in the container.
duzeltme.secenekler[3].text: $49.2\text{ atm}$; attractions between $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molecules reduce the force of their collisions with the walls.
duzeltme.aciklama:
1. $T=27+273=300\text{ K}$.
2. $P_{ideal}=\dfrac{nRT}{V}=\dfrac{(1.00)(0.08206)(300)}{0.500}=49.2\text{ atm}$.
3. Ölçülen basınç daha düşük → $\mathrm{CO_2}$ molekülleri arasındaki LDF çekimleri (22 elektron, büyük ve kutuplanabilir elektron bulutu) duvar çarpışmalarını zayıflatır.
